title: RENUMAR — De minute en minute 2.0 (Ressources NUMériques pour l'édition des Archives de la Renaissance)
institution: Centre d'Études Supérieures de la Renaissance (CESR), Université de Tours, with MSH Val de Loire and the Archives départementales de l'Indre-et-Loire and du Cher
notes:
Database of transcriptions and/or structured analyses of Renaissance archival acts (notarial minutes, municipal deliberations and correspondence, fiscal registers) mainly from Tours/Touraine, Bourges and Paris; documents run from 1462 with about 1% of entries analysing 18th-century acts. The project states 21,161 analyses or transcriptions as of 1 September 2025 (source: project 'Base' page, https://renumar.univ-tours.fr/base/; a 4 May 2026 update added 5,200+ entries); many entries are analyses rather than full transcriptions, so the count overstates full-text coverage, and no word count is published. The underlying data is encoded in XML-TEI (migration begun 2011, searched via XTF) but no downloadable files were found, so the published format is HTML. The original base was compiled by Pierre Aquilon and Bernard Chevalier.

Justification: A freely accessible, actively maintained (updated 4 May 2026) digital edition/database of transcribed Renaissance archival documents (notarial acts) from the CESR, University of Tours, squarely within 1450–1700; not in the catalogue (the catalogued BVH–Épistomon record covers the BVH literary text corpus, a different collection). Found via a general web search for new French digital editions of 16th-century sources (École des chartes event listing).
Found at: https://www.chartes.psl.eu/gazette-chartiste/agenda/de-nouvelles-sources-en-ligne-pour-lhistoire-de-france-du-xvie-s
